reasoning_summary: Statistical quality is good. The stationary window holds 12 cycles. Mean Cd is 1.2901 with a 95% CI of 5.2336e-05 and relative drift of 0.00016636. St is 0.15848 from the time-domain estimate and 0.15849 from the FFT. The Cl amplitude of 0.25631 against an rms of 0.18121 is consistent with a sinusoid.

The setup is sound. Re is 100 with a uniform inlet (ux_nonuniformity 0.0). The domain is 30D upstream, 50D downstream and 40D half-height, so blockage is 0.0125. The outlet and pressure BCs are standard. The force reference values (magUInf 0.15, lRef 0.01, Aref 0.0001) match the problem. checkMesh passes, and mass imbalance is 2.5e-10.

These checks only show that the run was run correctly. They do not show that it is accurate to 3%. There is only one run, so there is no mesh or time-step refinement study and no independent reference in the evidence. Discretisation bias is therefore unquantified.

Several features could cause a bias of a few percent. The mesh is modest at 30580 cells with a representative size of 0.45745 D. The wake is coarse at its far end (wake_last_cell_D 1.0209). Time integration is first-order Euler with a max Courant number of 2.9248. The FFT frequency resolution is 0.013333, which is about 8% of St, so the St figure relies on the time-domain estimate. The stationary-window start sits at the MSER cap (73.298), which is a minor flag.
I see no clear defect that would justify REJECT, and no convergence evidence that would justify ACCEPT. Confidence in either direction is low.
